findings.element: Invoices tab → Invoice date lock note ('To change it, change Schedule start date.') together with RevRec → Schedule start date
findings.finding: The lock note says changing Schedule start date unlocks Invoice date, but changing it to Invoice issued date (the option a user picks to move to issued dates) keeps Invoice date locked on Created, so the escape path loops back to the same lock.
findings.user_impact: A RevRec user who wants Stripe invoices on the issued date follows the note, confirms Invoice issued date, comes back and finds Invoice date still locked on Created. The only real way out is switching RevRec to Payment date, which the note doesn't mention and which re-dates new schedules. Many users will stall here, or leave books on Created while schedules start on Issued.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the lock note say exactly which Schedule start value releases the lock (Payment date), or name the path that gets both settings onto the issued date, so following the link can't end in the same locked state.

evidence.action: Org RevRec · invoice → Invoices tab (select disabled, value 'created', lock note shown) → clicked the lock-note link 'Schedule start date' → picked Invoice issued date → Change (statemap: value 'issued') → back to 1 · Invoices. The return step isn't in the state map, so it was re-run in a headless browser against the live prototype.
evidence.observed: After the return, inv-date is still disabled=true with value 'created', and the same note reads 'Locked while Revenue Recognition starts schedules from the invoice date. To change it, change Schedule start date.' This matches rrLock() in the prototype source (locked whenever schedule !== 'payment') and the spec's lock rule. The state map's cross-screen zone only records the Payment date case (unlocked).

findings.element: RevRec → Schedule start date confirmation dialog ('Change schedule start date?')
findings.finding: The confirmation dialog only talks about new and existing schedules. It never says that the choice also locks the Stripe Invoice date (Invoice created/issued date) or unlocks it (Payment date), and that cross-screen effect is the main thing this change does to the other settings.
findings.user_impact: Users confirm the change without knowing it takes control of the Stripe Invoice date. They find out later as an unexplained disabled control on a different screen, which undercuts the 'understand what that choice changes' part of the primary task.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause to the dialog body, chosen by the picked option, saying whether the Stripe Invoice date will be locked or editable after the change.

evidence.action: RevRec settings: picked Invoice issued date in Schedule start date. Then the cross-screen case: Schedule start = Payment date → Invoices tab.
evidence.observed: Dialog text is 'New schedules will start from the invoice issued date. Existing schedules keep their current dates until they're rebuilt — contact support to rebuild them.' with Cancel / Change and no mention of Invoice date. The state map records that the Invoices lock is derived from the current Schedule start (Payment date → enabled=true, no lock note; Invoice created date → disabled with lock note).

findings.element: Sync details → Issued date row in example B (synced on created date)
findings.finding: When the invoice was synced on the created date, the Date in books row disappears but the Issued date row stays. The panel then shows two dates and doesn't say which one went to the books.
findings.user_impact: A user reconciling a period sees Issued date Jan 6, 2026 next to Transaction date Dec 28, 2025 and can't tell which month the entry landed in. Telling those apart is the whole reason the new rows exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the Date in books row in both cases, showing the created date with its 'per Invoice date setting' note when the setting is Created, so the books date is always stated.

evidence.action: Sync details: switched the Example from A (synced on issued date) to B (synced on created date).
evidence.observed: In A: 'Issued date Jan 6, 2026 · 09:40' and 'Date in books Jan 6, 2026 · issued date, per Invoice date setting'. In B: 'Transaction date Dec 28, 2025 · 10:12' and 'Issued date Jan 6, 2026 · 09:40' are still shown, and the 'Date in books' row disappears.
